notes:
Summary: Vesper Health DataWorks evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production clinical assistant (HIPAA-adjacent workflows). Strong preference for dedicated capacity + VPC. Very focused on deterministic latency and SLA guarantees — procurement/legal driving high bar for uptime + credits. 

Sales notes (choppy):
- First contact Q4 2025, POC ran Jan 2026 against anonymized clinical dialogs. Good quality, need perf tuning.
- Chief infra ask: guaranteed throughput for peak batch inference windows (overnight chart scoring) + low-latency interactive chat for clinicians.
- "We cannot have patient-facing timeouts during clinic hours" — Head of Platform.
- Legal pushing hard on uptime % and credit matrix. They want 99.99% or contractual financial offset that scales.
- Security completed SOC2 questions; ISO27001 evidence required. KMS + HSM integration discussed.
- Data residency: must keep logs in US-East region and provide retention controls for 7 years (audit).
- Budget: procurement team expects committed reserved capacity and predictable monthly invoice (prefers annual commit).
- Internal champion: Dir. ML Ops (Eva Monroe) — wants 8xA100 reserved with 4-node burst for scheduled overnight throughput.

Short fragments often used in companion notes. See Drive links for SOW draft and legal redline.
timeline: 2026-01-26 POC performance review (good accuracy; latency spikes for long context)

sla_requirements: Requested SLA summary from Vesper: uptime 99.99% (monthly), credit schedule: 5% monthly credit for 99.9-99.99, 15% for 99.0-99.9, 50% for <99.0; maintenance windows: prefer 0200-0500 local (US-EAST) weekly with 30 days notice; support: P0/P1 acknowledgement 15 minutes, P2 response 1 hour, on-call 24/7 for incident escalations; RPO/RTO expectations for private control plane: RTO <1h for control-plane failures. Vesper requested contractual SLOs for p50/p95 generation latency for short-chat path (p50 <80ms, p95 <220ms) and committed throughput floor of 1.2M tokens/hour for peak ETL/overnight jobs.
reserved_gpu_plan: Vesper proposes reserved pool: 8xA100-80GB (production), 4xA100 burst (buffer), network egress within VPC, dedicated NVMe for KV cache. Autoscaling guardrails: no more than 2x burst without manual approval. Prefer monthly billing with annual commit discount. Need explicit SKU list in SOW and proof of node pinning during scheduled clinic hours.
throughput_latency_targets: Throughput: sustained 1.2M tokens/hr for nightly batch (jobs window 00:00-06:00 EST), burst 2.2M tokens/hr for 30-minute spikes. Latency SLOs for interactive: p50 <80ms, p90 <150ms, p95 <220ms for 128-token prompts. Must include measurement methodology (client-side vs server-side timings) and sampling frequency. Cache warming for KV/prefix reuse to be included with baseline measurements.
negotiation_points: Uptime target: Redwood standard 99.9% -> Vesper asking 99.99%: debate on credit % and financial exposure
Credit schedule: Vesper wants progressive credits up to 50% for large outages; Redwood needs cap and operational carve-outs (force majeure, customer misconfig)
Maintenance windows: Vesper wants limited maintenance during clinic hours; Redwood requests 6-hour weekly window for kernel upgrades (propose weekends) with 30-day notice
Support SLAs: P1 15m ack vs Redwood standard 30m; propose escalation path (AE->SE->SRE) and optional premium on-call package
Throughput guarantees: define test harness and acceptance criteria for baseline throughput; tie credits only if Redwood fails synthetic throughput tests during agreed test windows
quotes: "If clinic workflows stall for >60s, we have compliance exposure. Need deterministic guarantees." — Eva Monroe (Dir. ML Ops)
"We expect an enterprise contract with financial recourse tied to availability. Credits are fine but need to be meaningful." — Vesper Legal
